blocks.text: **One tag, one job.** Everything in these boxes is a tag with an NFC sticker inside. Tap it with a phone and it does one thing: opens a page, books a meeting, joins the Wi-Fi. Here are the eight jobs in the Tilde booth’s boxes, what each does on an iPhone and on Android, and how to make your own.

items.text: **The sticker does the work.** A tap opens whatever was written to it. The other phone doesn’t need an app.
**Any phone with NFC.** Many Android phones have NFC off until you turn it on, and older iPhones (7 to X) need the NFC reader in Control Center.
**You write it.** Tilde for Android writes any of these in a few taps, for free: Cards → **Write a sticker**, then choose what it opens. On an iPhone, the free NFC Tools app writes a link.
**You can rewrite it.** A phone rewrites the sticker through the plastic, so a tag can change jobs.
**Anything on a tag is public.** Anyone who taps it can read it and copy what’s on it. Put on it only what you’d put on a poster.

blocks.text: **The code on the booth’s tags:** some of the booth’s tags have a QR code on the front. It opens Tilde’s page (`taptilde.com`), not what’s on your sticker. A tag you print yourself carries your own link in its code.
the two giveaway boxes, open: four stacks each
The booth’s giveaway tags are khaki on black, with each job’s icon on the back.
**A tap opens your website, your LinkedIn or any page.**

items.text: **Android and iPhone:** a tap opens the link. No typing a URL.
**Make one:** add the link to a card on the Cards tab, then **Write a sticker** and choose it. On an iPhone, write it with NFC Tools.
**Keep in mind:** use it for yourself too, as a physical bookmark for a page you open every day (see below).
**Android and iPhone:** a tap opens your booking page (Calendly, Google Calendar’s booking pages or any other).
**Make one:** add your booking link to a card, then **Write a sticker** and choose it.
**Keep in mind:** use a booking page that shows only your free times, never your calendar’s details.

blocks.text: **A tap opens a WhatsApp chat with you, with a greeting ready to send. No more “text me your number”.**

items.text: **Android and iPhone:** a tap opens WhatsApp on a chat with you, the greeting filled in.
**Make one:** add **WhatsApp** to a card, then **Write a sticker → WhatsApp**.
**Keep in mind:** the link carries your number, so anyone who taps it can message you.
**Android:** a tap offers to save your contact card, if it fits the sticker.
**iPhone:** iPhones open links from a tap, not contact cards. For iPhone users, use the Link tag with your website.
**Make one:** **Write a sticker → Contact card**. An NTAG216 sticker holds a full contact card.
**Keep in mind:** anyone who taps it gets your contact card. In Edit card, uncheck your phone number or email under **What they save** if you’d rather leave them off.

blocks.text: **Friends over? They tap the tag and they’re online. No asking for the password, no typing.**

items.text: **Android:** a tap offers to connect to your network, and joins.
**iPhone:** iPhones can’t join from a tag: they scan the Wi-Fi code on your phone’s Share screen.
**Make one:** set up **Guest Wi-Fi** in Tilde’s Settings, then **Write a sticker → Guest Wi-Fi** (it’s named **Wi-Fi** if you’ve set up Hotspot too).
**Keep in mind:** use your guest network, never your main one. Anyone with the tag can read the password.

blocks.text: **Found this? Tap to call the owner.** For your keys or your bag.

items.text: **Android:** a tap opens the phone app with your number filled in, ready to call.
**iPhone:** iPhones can’t call from this tag yet: it’s for Android phones.
**Make one:** in Tilde, make a card with your number, then **Write a sticker → Phone number** and pick **Call**.
**Keep in mind:** never an address. Keys plus an address is a way in. A first name helps whoever finds it.

blocks.text: **If your child loses their phone, whoever finds them taps the tag on their backpack, and your number is ready to call.**

items.text: **Android:** a tap opens the phone app with your number filled in, ready to call. No internet needed.
**iPhone:** iPhones can’t call from this tag yet: it’s for Android phones.
**Make one:** in Tilde, make a card with one parent’s number, then **Write a sticker → Phone number** and pick **Call**.
**Keep in mind:** one parent’s number is enough. Don’t put on it the child’s name, school or address, or your own address: anyone who finds it can read it.

blocks.text: **One tap and your number is ready to call, or a new text to you, without saving a contact.**

items.text: **Android:** a tap opens the dialer with your number filled in (Call), or a new text to you (Text).
**iPhone:** iPhones scan the code on your phone’s screen instead.
**Make one:** **Write a sticker → Phone number**, then pick **Text** or **Call**.
**Keep in mind:** the text starts empty, and Call only fills in the number: nobody’s phone calls you by itself.

blocks.text: The shopping list on the fridge
the grocery list on a fridge
**Tap the list on the fridge, and it’s on your phone.** Coming in the next app update.

items.text: **Android and iPhone:** a tap opens the list on a page, with tick boxes, and no app is needed. Your ticks stay on your phone; they don’t change the list on the fridge.
**Make one:** make the list in Tilde, then **Write a sticker** to the Grocery list (see [Home & desk](/tilde/home#grocery-list)). To change it, edit it in Tilde and tap the sticker again.
**Keep in mind:** anyone who taps it can read the list.

blocks.text: **Flip to the tag, tap, and it’s open.** A ring of thin tags works like index cards, each for a page you’d otherwise dig for: the parcel you’re tracking, today’s forecast, your gym’s schedule. These are for you rather than to share. Your phone rewrites a tag when the parcel changes, without a reprint.
**The demo keychain:** flip through and tap any. At the booth, its tags open things like these:

blocks.text: A tracking page can show your name and address on some carriers’ sites, so keep those bookmarks on your own keys.
You don’t need a tag at all: Tilde shares from your phone with a tap or a code.

items.text: **Keep a card for every room:** a work card with your title and LinkedIn, and a socials card without your number.
**Remember who you met:** Met lists every tap of your phone, with the time, the card and the event. Add a note, then go through it after the event.
**At the Tilde booth at Web Summit:** take a tag from the boxes. It’s written for you there, in about 10 seconds.
**Print your own:** coins and tags from [github.com/tbutman/tilde-card](https://github.com/tbutman/tilde-card).
**Or any NFC sticker:** Tilde writes the same things to a plain round NFC sticker, or to a Tilde Card.
